MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility, unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: distraction, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Radio negotiation at very close range
- Channel selection consumes remaining time
- Each vessel waits for the other to resolve risk
Investigator finding: The pilots attempted to communicate their way out of danger and each hoped the other would resolve the situation instead of making an immediate effective decision.
Transferable lesson: Do not let radio coordination or equipment manipulation displace timely collision-avoidance decisions when time is critical.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not imply that useful, timely radio coordination should be avoided.
Source quotations:
- Page 16: There was an attempt by both pilots to communicate their way out of trouble
- Page 17: Both were hoping for the other to do something to resolve the situation.

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- Predicted meeting at a channel constriction
- Obstruction limits passing room
Investigator finding: The vessels met at a recognised pinch point where prudent navigation should have anticipated and avoided the meeting.
Transferable lesson: Project meeting locations as well as closest approach, accounting for local constrictions when planning encounters.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The pinch-point analogy does not directly transfer to unrestricted open water.
Source quotations:
- Page 11: Prudent navigation would have established that the ships were going to meet in this area and appropriate action taken to avoid meeting there.

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Making way in fog without sound signals
Investigator finding: Neither vessel gave sound signals; these could have indicated closing traffic and prompted greater caution.
Transferable lesson: Include the required restricted-visibility sound signals in the collision-avoidance routine rather than relying solely on radar or radio.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Sound signals do not replace radar assessment or establish a precise contact solution.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: Neither vessel was giving sound signals.
- Page 12: The sound signal would have served as an indicator that the ships were closing

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility, unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Point-to-point buoy navigation
- Little long-range scanning
- Radar mapping available but unused
Investigator finding: Navigation concentrated on successive buoys, while radar mapping could have shown both vessels relative to safe-water contours and hazards.
Transferable lesson: Maintain a broader passage and traffic picture rather than focusing solely on the next mark; use suitable available radar monitoring aids.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Radar mapping depends on suitable equipment and appropriate map information; it is not a substitute for contact assessment.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: the ships were simply steered point to point with no use made of parallel indexing, or little use of long range scanning.
- Page 14: Radar mapping facilities are excellent tools, which help observers remain aware of their position relative to surface and seabed hazards.

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Electronic chart position appears to overswing during rapid manoeuvring
Investigator finding: Although not causal here, the investigation warned that GPS and electronic-chart smoothing can create misleading apparent position excursions during course changes.
Transferable lesson: Cross-check electronic position indications with other means when rapid changes in motion could make the display misleading.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report did not identify the electronic chart system as an influencing factor in this collision.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: Time constants set into GPS receivers and ECD systems to smooth the position can produce apparent over swings on ECDs when changing course
- Page 14: Other means should be used to cross-check positions .

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Synthetic ship symbol places radar origin at the wrong location
Investigator finding: An incorrect synthetic radar-origin depiction was not causal here but could mislead an operator in other circumstances.
Transferable lesson: Verify display reference points before using close-range radar geometry to judge clearance.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This discrepancy was explicitly assessed as having no bearing on this accident.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: showing the radar trace origin as being placed on the bow of the ship when in fact it was near the stern
- Page 15: could provide an operator with misleading information in other circumstances.

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- Course corrections attributed to assumed tidal set
- Observed track does not support the assumed current
Investigator finding: The pilot manoeuvred to counter a perceived tidal set, although the evidence indicated effectively slack water and a correction for earlier helm instead.
Transferable lesson: Check environmental explanations for observed motion against track evidence and recent control inputs before basing further action on them.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not establish that tidal set is negligible at another time or location.
Source quotations:
- Page 17: the subsequent port helm appears to be a correction for the effect of the earlier starboard helm and not the effect of the tide as the pilot believed.
- Page 17: it was effectively slack water, with little or no cross channel set.

report_title: Skagern and Samskip Courier Report No 6/2007
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility, unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Vessel crosses to the other side of a narrow channel to avoid a perceived hazard
Investigator finding: Samskip Courier failed to keep to her side of the channel while attempting to counter the perceived set towards the light float.
Transferable lesson: Assess a hazard-avoidance proposal against its effect on channel position and approaching traffic, not just clearance from the individual hazard.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The channel-side finding does not assign encounter roles in open water or establish a particular manoeuvre elsewhere.
Source quotations:
- Page 9: Samskip Courier failed to keep to the starboard side of the channel as she approached and rounded Sand End light float.
- Page 12: The vessel was allowed to cross over to apparently avoid being set onto the Sand End light float with the flood tide.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- Traffic prompts a departure from the passage plan.
- The revised track approaches a navigational hazard or remains in a separation zone.
Investigator finding: The early alteration for traffic was justified, but its execution took the ship too close to the lightfloat and unnecessarily prolonged its presence in the separation zone.
Transferable lesson: Assess the whole track of a traffic-driven passage-plan deviation, including clearance from hazards and routeing constraints, rather than judging it only by its immediate traffic benefit.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific lightfloat and separation-zone concerns do not transfer to waters without comparable hazards or routeing constraints.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: While the early alteration of course was a justifiable action, the execution of the manoeuvre was not best carried out, by passing too close to the lightfloat and staying in the separation zone too long without reason.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- A proposed passing route is constrained by an assumed shoal-water limit.
- Radar waypoints and track lines dominate the navigation assessment.
- Available safe sea room has not been checked against the chart.
Investigator finding: The master mistakenly believed that shallow water prevented using sea room to the west. Investigators considered that greater focus on radar track information than on the chart might have impaired his awareness of safe navigation areas.
Transferable lesson: Verify actual navigable sea room against charted hazards before rejecting alternative passing space; radar route guidance alone should not determine the boundaries of a collision-avoidance manoeuvre.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not establish that apparently available water is safe elsewhere; actual depth, hazards and vessel constraints must support that assessment.
- The suggested over-reliance on radar information was a qualified finding, not a proven certainty.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: This was a mistaken assumption and he could have safely gone in that direction. The chart was not marked with no-go areas.
- Page 15: The master might not have been fully aware of his ship’s position in relation to areas of safe navigation, because he might have been more focused on the radar track information than the chart.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact, overtaking
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- A proposal routes the vessel between two contacts.
- The proposed passage leaves little allowance for unexpected contact motion.
Investigator finding: Passing between Nordheim and the fishing vessel left little margin for error and was identified as a cause of the collision.
Transferable lesson: Assess a proposed passage between contacts for its margin against unforeseen developments, not merely whether it fits their present tracks.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The finding does not establish that every passage between contacts is unsafe; the analogy weakens where there is ample clearance and contingency space.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: By deciding to go between the two vessels, the master left little margin for error if something unforeseen happened.
- Page 15: Pasadena Universal’s master attempted to pass between Nordheim and the fishing vessel, leaving little margin for error.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, multi_contact
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- The proposed passing plan depends on another vessel maintaining its current course.
- An intervening course alteration would consume the available passing clearance.
Investigator finding: The master failed to anticipate Nordheim's alteration and wrongly assumed that she would maintain course while he passed between the vessels.
Transferable lesson: Test whether a passing proposal remains adequately separated if another vessel alters course, rather than treating its present course as guaranteed.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This finding does not predict that another vessel will alter course or prescribe a particular avoiding manoeuvre.
- The specific concern is less applicable where the proposal does not depend on the other vessel maintaining course.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: The master failed to anticipate Nordheim’s alteration of course to starboard and erroneously assumed that she would remain on her course during the time he would pass between the two vessels.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, poor_team_coordination
Warning signs:
- An approaching vessel has not been reported to the watchkeeper.
- A lookout is posted, but the bridge team's contact picture is incomplete.
- A vessel approaches from a quarter not represented in the watchkeeper's assessment.
Investigator finding: Nordheim's bridge team did not maintain a proper lookout. The lookout failed to report Pasadena Universal, and the chief officer remained unaware of her approach.
Transferable lesson: Ensure that lookout observations reach the watchkeeper and form a complete contact picture; merely posting a lookout does not establish that approaching traffic is being detected and reported.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This finding does not establish a lookout-reporting failure where all relevant contacts are already detected, reported and understood.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: The lookout had not reported the approach of Pasadena Universal.
- Page 14: The bridge team was not keeping a proper lookout under Rule 5 of the Collision Regulations.
- Page 15: The chief officer was unaware of the approach of Pasadena Universal.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- A nearby contact is assumed to be a vessel observed earlier.
- Visual observations and reported ranges do not form a consistent contact history.
- Several overtaking contacts could be confused.
Investigator finding: The chief officer confused the approaching Pasadena Universal with a different overtaking vessel that remained more than six miles away. That mistaken association contributed to his belief that altering course was safe.
Transferable lesson: Reconcile contact identity, range and observed movement before using an earlier sighting to justify a manoeuvre, particularly when several vessels could match the description.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The contact-confusion analogy does not apply where identity and motion history are reliably established and mutually consistent.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: At 2124, the other ship was 7.4 miles away and at the time of the collision she was 6.2 miles away.
- Page 14: He wrongly assumed that this was the ship that he was in collision with.
- Page 14: Although the chief officer was aware of an overtaking ship about 1 mile astern, it is apparent that he did not appreciate her rapid speed of approach and that his visual observation, of what he assumed to be the same ship some 6 miles on the starboard quarter, convinced him that it was safe to alter course to starboard at that time.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- A navigational alteration is proposed while another vessel is overtaking nearby.
- The approaching vessel's closing rate has not been appreciated.
- The timing of a planned alteration is based on position alone rather than developing proximity.
Investigator finding: Nordheim altered course while Pasadena Universal was overtaking at close proximity. The chief officer did not appreciate her rapid approach; awareness of it could have preserved the option of delaying the navigational alteration.
Transferable lesson: Before executing a navigational alteration, reassess nearby overtaking traffic and its rate of approach, including whether the timing of the alteration remains appropriate.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The finding does not prescribe delaying every planned alteration or maintaining course when that would be unsafe.
- Its specific timing lesson is less applicable when no approaching contact could be affected by the alteration.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: Nordheim’s chief officer altered course to starboard at a time when Pasadena Universal was overtaking at close proximity.
- Page 15: The chief officer did not appreciate Pasadena Universal’s rapid speed of approach.
- Page 14: Had he been aware of Pasadena Universal and her rapid speed of approach, he may have given himself the option of delaying the navigational alteration of course.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: role_confusion
Warning signs:
- An overtaking relationship is being used to frame decisions although the vessels are not in sight.
Investigator finding: The investigator considered restricted-visibility provisions pertinent because the vessels could not see each other, rather than the overtaking rule applicable to vessels in sight.
Transferable lesson: Establish whether vessels are in sight before applying overtaking-role assumptions to the collision-avoidance decision.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This restricted-visibility distinction does not transfer unchanged to vessels in sight of one another.
Source quotations:
- Page 11: Rule 13 of the Collision Regulations regarding overtaking is only applicable to vessels in sight each other.
- Page 11: As the vessels could not see each other, it is considered that Rule 19 governing the conduct of vessels in restricted visibility is pertinent.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- A passing assumption lacks a calculated passing time or distance.
- A proposed alteration has not been assessed for its effect on CPA.
Investigator finding: Wintertide's OOW did not determine when or where MSC Sabrina would pass and did not use the trial-manoeuvre facility before altering.
Transferable lesson: Establish CPA and TCPA from reliable plotting and assess the effect of a proposed manoeuvre before relying on an expected passing arrangement.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- A trial-manoeuvre facility cannot be assumed available on every installation; reliable assessment remains necessary by available means.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: Had he been using his display effectively and plotted MSC Sabrina correctly, this information would have been available from the TCPA and CPA readouts.
- Page 15: The chief officer did not utilise the 'trial manoeuvre' facility on his radar display prior to altering course.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Close-range contacts are manually plotted on a long radar range scale.
- CPA reassurance depends on imprecise target marking.
- Target motion may not have remained steady between plots.
Investigator finding: Inaccurate manual plotting on the six-mile range scale produced misleading CPA information and an incorrect expectation that MSC Sabrina would pass astern.
Transferable lesson: Treat manually derived CPA as conditional on plotting precision, suitable range scale, adequate plot interval and steady target motion; reassess rather than relying on uncertain clearance.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The manual target-marking mechanism does not directly describe automatic tracking, whose accuracy must be assessed on its own terms.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: The accuracy of the information displayed, such as course, speed, and CPA, relies on a reasonable time interval between manually injected plots, a reliance on the vessel being plotted maintaining a steady course and speed, and the accuracy of the plot by the operator.
- Page 17: Following the alteration, the plotting of MSC Sabrina by radar on a six-mile range scale was inaccurate. The resulting information led the OOW to incorrectly assume MSC Sabrina would pass under the stern.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- An initially acceptable CPA is being treated as a settled passing arrangement.
Investigator finding: The investigator considered the initial eight-cable passing distance reasonable only provided the overtaken vessel's movements were closely monitored.
Transferable lesson: An acceptable initial CPA does not remove the need to monitor the other vessel's movements and update the passing assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report's eight-cable assessment is not a universal minimum or assurance of safety in other circumstances.
Source quotations:
- Page 11: In this case, it is considered that 8 cables was a reasonable distance to pass another vessel in a traffic lane, providing the movements of the vessel being overtaken were closely monitored.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, emergency, recovery
Causal mechanisms: distraction, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- A collision or close encounter diverts attention from another nearby contact.
- Manoeuvring and communications compete with radar monitoring.
Investigator finding: Distraction following the Concordia collision prevented MSC Sabrina's OOW from detecting Wintertide's alteration and steady bearing.
Transferable lesson: Preserve radar monitoring of remaining traffic while handling an incident, manoeuvring and making communications.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The multi-contact distraction mechanism is not established where no other traffic requires monitoring.
Source quotations:
- Page 17: A proper radar lookout was not maintained; the OOW was distracted by the collision with Concordia and did not detect that Wintertide had altered course and was on a steady bearing.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Visibility is diminishing without a speed reassessment.
- Stopping distance and turning advance exceed the visual detection distance.
Investigator finding: MSC Sabrina's speed was unsafe in the prevailing visibility and left insufficient opportunity for effective avoiding action when the risk became apparent.
Transferable lesson: Assess speed against visibility and the vessel's stopping and turning capabilities before close quarters develop.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The reported speed and manoeuvring distances are vessel- and condition-specific, not universal thresholds.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: Both distances were beyond the prevailing visibility at the time of the collision.
- Page 17: A speed of 17.5 knots was not a safe speed in the prevailing visibility. It was too fast to enable sufficient avoiding action to be taken, when the risk of collision became apparent

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- A speed reduction is proposed with another vessel already very close astern or alongside.
Investigator finding: Despite MSC Sabrina's excessive earlier speed, the investigator considered immediate pre-impact speed reduction inappropriate in the actual relative positions; Wintertide also had a vessel too close astern for a late reduction.
Transferable lesson: Distinguish timely safe-speed management from a late emergency speed change; assess the latter against current relative positions and courses rather than assuming reduction is always beneficial.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not justify maintaining excessive speed earlier or establish that speed reduction is generally inappropriate in emergencies.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: it would have been inappropriate to reduce speed with another vessel so close astern.
- Page 14: The master’s decision not to reduce speed at this stage was prudent, given the relative positions and courses of the two . vessels;

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, poor_team_coordination
Warning signs:
- No helmsman is stationed despite restricted-visibility orders.
- Emergency helm action requires the OOW to move and change steering mode.
- The steering mode is not confirmed when helm is ordered.
Investigator finding: Wintertide's avoiding action was delayed by moving to the helm and changing to hand steering; required helmsmen might have improved response on both ships, and MSC Sabrina's actual helm application was uncertain.
Transferable lesson: Establish required helm readiness before an emergency and confirm the control mode when ordering avoiding action.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific delay does not transfer where a helmsman is already ready and the steering mode and helm response are confirmed.
Source quotations:
- Page 16: Avoiding action was delayed while the OOW moved from the port bridge wing to the helm and changed to hand steering.
- Page 14: With helmsmen on the helm as required by company orders, the response by both vessels might have been quicker.
- Page 14: it cannot be established exactly how, or what amount of helm, was applied.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: emergency
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- An emergency propulsion change is proposed without considering its effect on steering or transverse thrust.
Investigator finding: Wintertide's emergency propulsion choice preserved steering effectiveness; stopping or using astern propulsion could have produced less favourable steering or bow movement in that situation.
Transferable lesson: Evaluate emergency propulsion and helm together, accounting for their effect on steering effectiveness and vessel-specific transverse thrust.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The particular propulsion effects and favourable direction of bow movement cannot be assumed for another vessel or encounter geometry.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: Had the propeller pitch been put to Stop, the steering might have been less effective, and the paddlewheel effect caused by any astern movement on the engines would have caused the bows to pay off to starboard, towards MSC Sabrina.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Targets are displayed but not systematically tracked.
- Bearing and range observations are not being converted into a collision-risk assessment.
Investigator finding: Strilmøy used no radar plotting technique constituting systematic observation of detected objects.
Transferable lesson: Treat radar detection as the start of assessment: systematically monitor target movement using suitable plotting or equivalent observation.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Absence of ARPA alone does not establish this failure if another effective systematic observation method is being used.
Source quotations:
- Page 18: The OOW on Strilmøy was not using any radar plotting technique that could be considered a systematic observation of detected objects
- Page 14: It is the monitoring of the target’s movement that will indicate the possible risk of collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Collision risk is inferred only from true trails or estimated future positions.
Investigator finding: True trails show target heading but do not directly indicate collision risk; estimating risk from true-vector information was described as imprecise and inappropriate.
Transferable lesson: Do not use true trails alone as a substitute for a systematic relative-motion and collision-risk assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This criticism does not transfer to the mere display of true trails alongside an effective independent collision-risk assessment.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: The true trail function will only indicate where a target is heading, and will not directly indicate any risk of collision.
- Page 15: It is a very imprecise and inappropriate method of determining if risk of collision exists.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Available ARPA acquisition and CPA/TCPA warning functions are unused.
Investigator finding: ARPA could have provided systematic observations and an alarm when preset CPA/TCPA limits were encroached upon, but its functions were not used.
Transferable lesson: Use available target-acquisition and CPA/TCPA warning functions to support systematic monitoring rather than leaving their protective capability unused.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This specific capability does not transfer to equipment without these functions; alarms are not presented as a replacement for lookout.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: By using ARPA, systematic observations are carried out automatically for the observer.
- Page 15: an alarm would have been set to sound when the target information showed that the TCPA and CPA had encroached within pre-set limits.
- Page 15: In Strilmøy, the ARPA functions were not being used.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: role_confusion, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Fishing status is being treated as a right to maintain course and speed in a radar-only encounter.
Investigator finding: The fishing vessels mistakenly considered that they had right of way in restricted visibility; both sides should have acted before coming into sight.
Transferable lesson: Do not import in-sight stand-on expectations into a restricted-visibility encounter where vessels are not in sight of one another.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Once vessels are in sight, the applicable role framework must be reassessed; this finding does not remove in-sight responsibilities.
Source quotations:
- Page 16: They mistakenly (since it was restricted visibility) considered that they had the right of way.
- Page 15: At that stage, Strilmøy and the fishing vessels should have taken action to avoid collision. Neither side did.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: stand_on
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, rigid_stand_on_interpretation
Warning signs:
- The vessel required to keep clear is not taking sufficient action.
- Visual acquisition occurs only at very close range.
Investigator finding: After visual contact, Harvester could have acted when Strilmøy's insufficient action became apparent, but very close range left little assessment time.
Transferable lesson: Stand-on status is not a reason to disregard another vessel's failure to act; recognise how little decision time may remain after late visual acquisition.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The stand-on aspect does not transfer to vessels not in sight or to encounters where that role has not been established.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: Harvester could have taken action once it became apparent that Strilmøy was not taking sufficient action.
- Page 15: There was, however, little time to make this assessment, as the vessels were, by then, at very close range.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- A proposed manoeuvre is being judged without accounting for towing resistance, slow response or gear hazards.
Investigator finding: Towing affected both the speed and effectiveness of Harvester's available actions, leaving insufficient time for a course alteration once Strilmøy emerged from fog.
Transferable lesson: Assess a proposal against the vessel's actual towing response and gear constraints, and allow sufficient time for the action to take effect.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific response and gear hazards do not transfer to vessels not towing or to different gear arrangements without supporting evidence.
Source quotations:
- Page 16: Altering course at the time Strilmøy first appeared from the fog would have allowed insufficient time for the alteration to take effect, due to the slow speed and the fact that she was towing.
- Page 16: This would, however, increase the chance that the propeller would be fouled by the gear.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- Autopilot remains engaged during an urgent manoeuvre.
- A control input does not produce the intended response.
Investigator finding: Autopilot limited Harvester's alteration and blocked Strilmøy's initial pod adjustment.
Transferable lesson: Check that the current control mode will execute the intended avoiding action; do not assume a control input guarantees the required manoeuvring response.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The particular control restrictions and response differences are equipment-specific and must not be assumed for other installations.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: because they were steering in autopilot, this action was blocked until an adjustment of greater than 60º was attempted.
- Page 17: If the steering had been in hand control, rather than in autopilot, hard-over helm could have been applied and a more significant alteration made before the collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Traffic is first recognised at a range leaving only seconds to act.
- An emergency stopping capability is relied upon despite inadequate detection time.
Investigator finding: Strilmøy's late detection left insufficient time for avoiding action, and its emergency action only slightly reduced the impact.
Transferable lesson: Judge available manoeuvring capability against detection range and remaining time; rapid manoeuvrability cannot compensate for recognition after the avoidance window has closed.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The reported distances and outcome are not stopping or collision thresholds for another vessel or encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: Harvester was not noticed by the OOW until approximately 50 metres ahead of Strilmøy, by which time any action taken by Strilmøy was too late to avoid a collision.
- Page 17: The action taken by Strilmøy was very late, and resulted only in a slightly reduced impact.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Vessels are operating in fog without required sound signals.
Investigator finding: The vessels were not sounding the required fog signals.
Transferable lesson: Include required fog signalling in the restricted-visibility operating state rather than treating radar monitoring as the whole response.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The fog-signalling finding does not apply outside conditions requiring those signals; the passages do not establish that signals alone would have prevented this collision.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: Under Rule 35 of the COLREGS all three vessels should have been sounding fog signals, but were not.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Own vessel is turning near anchored traffic
- Contact position or aspect changes during the turn
Investigator finding: Continuous visual and radar observation, together with monitoring of own heading and projected track, could have provided early warning during the turn.
Transferable lesson: Continue contact and projected-track monitoring throughout a turn rather than waiting until the new heading is established.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific turn-related analogy does not apply when own vessel is not manoeuvring near contacts.
Source quotations:
- Page 25: Visual and radar observation of the anchored vessels, and close monitoring of Global Mariner’s heading and projected track, throughout the turning manoeuvre would have enabled the master and the manoeuvring pilot to have been updated continuously on the current situation

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Possible anchor dragging
- Anchor watch has not detected movement
Investigator finding: If Atlantic Crusader was dragging before collision, the lack of awareness on her bridge indicated an inadequate anchor watch; whether she was dragging remains uncertain.
Transferable lesson: An anchored vessel's watch must actively verify that position is being maintained rather than assume the anchor is holding.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This is an anchor-watch lesson, not evidence that every apparently anchored contact is dragging.
- The report did not establish pre-collision dragging.
Source quotations:
- Page 31: If Atlantic Crusader was dragging her anchor before the collision, neither her watch officer nor her master was aware of the fact, which would indicate that an inadequate anchor watch was being maintained.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact, unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Unexpected contact aspect
- Apparent crossing motion conflicts with known anchorage status
- Bow or stern turbulence in strong current
Investigator finding: The initial belief that Atlantic Crusader was underway probably discouraged alternative explanations; current-induced turbulence could have made her appear to be manoeuvring.
Transferable lesson: Challenge an initial underway or crossing interpretation when position, aspect and environmental effects admit an anchored or dragging explanation.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This ambiguity is not a reason to reject reliable evidence that a vessel is underway.
- No definitive pre-collision movement scenario was established.
Source quotations:
- Page 26: This initial perception did not go unquestioned, but probably strongly influenced the rejection of any alternative explanation for her position and heading.
- Page 31: It is possible that turbulence at Atlantic Crusader’s bow and stern, because of the direction and strength of the current, gave the appearance that she was manoeuvring.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact, unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- Anchor status not visually checked
- Anchor ball or cable difficult to distinguish
- Anchor indication treated as proof of no movement
Investigator finding: Available binoculars were not used to check anchor indications, but even seeing an anchor ball or cable would not establish whether the vessel was moving.
Transferable lesson: Use available visual aids to check ambiguous status indications, while assessing actual movement separately from anchor status.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Visual confirmation may not be available in restricted visibility.
- An anchor indication alone cannot resolve whether a vessel is dragging.
Source quotations:
- Page 31: No attempt was made to use the available binoculars to establish whether Atlantic Crusader’s starboard anchor was deployed, or if the anchor ball was displayed forward.
- Page 31: However, sighting of the anchor ball, or starboard anchor cable alone, would have given no indication of her possible movement.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, distraction
Warning signs:
- VHF passing request substitutes for status verification
- Time spent establishing radio contact while risk develops
Investigator finding: The pilot used VHF instead of visually confirming status, and the analysis warned that radio contact attempts can waste time needed for compliance with the Collision Regulations.
Transferable lesson: Do not let VHF contact attempts or passing negotiations displace assessment and timely collision-avoidance duties.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not prohibit all VHF use or establish that a successful radio exchange would have prevented this collision.
Source quotations:
- Page 27: Instead of attempting to confirm by sight the status of Atlantic Crusader, the pilot used VHF radio to request a port to port passing.
- Page 27: valuable time can be wasted in trying to make contact instead of complying with the Collision Regulations.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: crossing
Vessel roles: stand_on
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: rigid_stand_on_interpretation
Warning signs:
- Other vessel is not taking appropriate avoiding action
Investigator finding: On the expressly hypothetical basis that both vessels were underway and crossing, the master was free to act when the other vessel was not taking appropriate action.
Transferable lesson: In an established stand-on crossing situation, do not interpret stand-on status as preventing action once the give-way vessel's failure to act appropriately is apparent.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report's crossing-role analysis was conditional; it does not assign those roles to an anchored contact or establish that Atlantic Crusader was underway.
Source quotations:
- Page 27: Global Mariner’s master was free to take avoiding action as soon as it became apparent that Atlantic Crusader was not taking appropriate action in compliance with the Rules.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Strong current
- Anchored contact and own vessel respond differently to current
Investigator finding: The current significantly reduced the time available for effective avoiding action, while the anchored vessel's response differed from that of the moving vessel.
Transferable lesson: Account explicitly for current and differing contact responses when judging the time available for effective action.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific current-driven time compression does not transfer to encounters without a material current effect.
Source quotations:
- Page 31: The strength and direction of the current significantly reduced the time available in which to take effective avoiding action.
- Page 31: Atlantic Crusader was at anchor and, therefore, apart from yawing, was not influenced by the current, except to the extent caused by any dragging.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, other
Warning signs:
- Unusual and confusing encounter
- Immediate collision risk
- Time needed to reinterpret the situation
Investigator finding: The unexpected situation required assessment time, and immediate collision risk probably increased stress with potential effects on appraisal and decision-making.
Transferable lesson: Allow for assessment and decision time when judging remaining action margins; an unexpected encounter may consume time even with active decision-makers.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not establish that stress impaired any particular decision or quantify a universal reaction-time allowance.
Source quotations:
- Page 32: Global Mariner’s master and manoeuvring pilot required time to assess the unusual, unexpected and confusing situation, and to decide on the avoiding action to be taken.
- Page 26: both the master and the manoeuvring pilot were probably experiencing increased levels of stress, which would have potentially affected their situation appraisal and decision-making ability.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Rapidly approaching radar contact
- Own vessel changing course without systematic target assessment
Investigator finding: The mate did not systematically plot the approaching ship on the fishing vessel's various courses.
Transferable lesson: Use systematic radar observation to reassess relative motion as own course changes; an intuitive sense that a contact is approaching is not a sufficient risk assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This failure mode does not apply where reliable systematic tracking is already maintained through own-vessel manoeuvres.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: The mate on the fishing vessel made no systematic plots of the movement of the radar echo of Celtic King when on these various courses

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: distraction, inadequate_cpa_assessment, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Target lost in clutter
- Time consumed trying to recover an echo
- Continued reliance on a lost target's previous CPA
Investigator finding: The chief officer spent valuable time searching for a lost echo while wrongly assuming that the fishing vessel would maintain course and cross ahead; the investigation called for caution and speed reduction.
Transferable lesson: Treat loss of a relevant radar track as increased uncertainty requiring reassessment of safe speed and cautious navigation, not as confirmation of the last predicted clearance; do not let echo recovery monopolise attention.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This lesson concerns loss of a relevant track without reliable alternative tracking, not a contact continuously confirmed by another dependable source.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: The chief officer spent valuable time (about 9 minutes) trying to find the echo, and he wrongly assumed that the fishing vessel would remain on course and cross ahead
- Page 13: Having lost the echo, it would have been wise for him to have reduced speed and navigated with caution

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Non-zero CPA accepted despite severely restricted visibility
- Sea room available but small clearing distances retained
Investigator finding: The clearing distances on the fishing vessel's various tracks were too small for severely restricted visibility with ample sea room.
Transferable lesson: Judge predicted clearance against visibility and available sea room rather than accepting a non-zero CPA as sufficient.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report supplies no universal minimum CPA; its assessment cannot be transferred as a numerical threshold to different visibility or sea-room conditions.
Source quotations:
- Page 16: The clearing distances for the various tracks were too small in severely restricted visibility and with plenty of sea room.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, other
Warning signs:
- Fog signals deferred because of an apparently comfortable CPA
- Signals begun only late in the encounter
Investigator finding: Both vessels omitted timely fog signals; the chief officer considered signals unnecessary because he expected a two-mile crossing ahead.
Transferable lesson: Do not make restricted-visibility sound signalling conditional on a threatening CPA or wait until a close-quarters situation develops.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This lesson concerns restricted-visibility signals, not signalling requirements in clear visibility.
Source quotations:
- Page 13: The chief officer assumed the fishing vessel was going to cross 2 miles ahead, and thought it was unnecessary to sound the fog signal for a vessel at that range.
- Page 17: The mate did not make any sound signals until the later stages of the incident.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact, overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- A successful prediction for one contact is reassuring the OOW about others.
- Observed passing distances or contact identities do not match earlier estimates.
Investigator finding: The officer gained confidence from one vessel passing clear, but the investigation concluded that the contacts he monitored were probably not Ash.
Transferable lesson: Verify each contact's identity and passing trend independently rather than extending reassurance from one successful passing prediction to other contacts.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This specific misidentification mechanism does not apply to a positively identified single-contact encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 22: this gave him some confidence that his estimation was correct.
- Page 22: the two vessels seen and monitored by the second officer were probably Danica Four and Rambler, and that Ash was not noticed until immediately before the collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- A contact may lie beneath the radar heading marker.
Investigator finding: The report identified heading-marker obscuration as a possible explanation for missing Ash's echo, not a proven cause.
Transferable lesson: Frequently suppress the heading marker temporarily to check for obscured targets.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This display-specific mechanism does not transfer where no marker obscures target information.
- Do not treat marker obscuration as established in this accident.
Source quotations:
- Page 23: one possible explanation of why the second officer did not readily notice it might be that it was partially obscured by the heading marker on the radar screen.
- Page 23: Every radar has the facility to temporarily switch off the heading marker on the screen so that operators can detect any targets that might be obscured and it is good practice to do this frequently during a watch.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: stand_on
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: distraction, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- A telephone call interrupts monitoring of an approaching vessel.
- Previous close overtaking is being used as reassurance.
Investigator finding: Ash's watchkeeper stopped monitoring the approach during a telephone call and consequently could not fulfil his stand-on obligations.
Transferable lesson: Preserve continuous monitoring of an overtaking vessel despite stand-on status, previous uneventful close passes, or non-navigational calls.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The stand-on obligations analogy requires an established stand-on relationship.
- The telephone mechanism does not apply where effective lookout coverage continues during the call.
Source quotations:
- Page 24: When the telephone rang he answered it, and had no view astern while he did so.
- Page 24: He had a duty to monitor the situation as Dutch Aquamarine approached.
- Page 27: He was therefore unaware of the developing situation and unable to fulfil his obligations as the stand-on vessel under the Collision Regulations.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact, overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: recovery, monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Track control is returning the vessel rapidly to its programmed track after avoidance.
- Returning to the track creates another close passing.
Investigator finding: Rapid return to programmed tracks helped perpetuate traffic bunching, and possible lack of proficiency with GPS and track-control functions contributed to this tendency.
Transferable lesson: Reassess surrounding traffic before restoring a programmed track after avoidance, and ensure the OOW understands the track-control functions being used.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The automatic-return mechanism does not apply when track control is not engaged.
- The report does not establish that every return to a planned track is unsafe.
Source quotations:
- Page 21: Dutch Aquamarine reverted to her track despite the fact that this meant that she passed Hornestrand at 1512 at a distance of only about 0.15 mile
- Page 27: It is possible that many navigators might not be fully adept in the use of GPS and track control systems, and this causes them to return to the programmed track after anti-collision manoeuvres.
- Page 27: This, in turn, tends to maintain the bunching of traffic on the popular pre-programmed tracks.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Markedly different speeds on coincident or near-coincident tracks.
Investigator finding: Speed differences on shared tracks increased the frequency of overtaking situations with conflict potential.
Transferable lesson: Treat substantial speed differences on a shared track as a reason to anticipate repeated overtaking conflicts, rather than regarding common direction of travel as reassuring.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This shared-track mechanism does not transfer to well-separated tracks without convergence.
- It does not predict that another encounter will end in collision.
Source quotations:
- Page 21: The greater the variation in speed among the vessels choosing this route, the more frequently overtaking situations with potential for conflict will occur.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: give_way, overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: action_required
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- An avoidance proposal would be late or difficult for the other vessel to perceive.
- Other contacts are being considered without identifying when effective action becomes available.
Investigator finding: Dutch Aquamarine should have acted once clear of other vessels, with an early, substantial and readily apparent action.
Transferable lesson: Assess avoidance proposals for timeliness, perceptibility and effects on other contacts, not merely whether they might eventually pass clear.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific finding that manoeuvring room was available does not transfer to encounters constrained by other traffic or navigation hazards.
Source quotations:
- Page 25: it is vitally important for the give-way vessel to give a clear early indication to the stand-on vessel that proper action is being taken to avoid a collision.
- Page 25: Dutch Aquamarine should have altered her course as soon as she was able, without affecting other vessels.
- Page 25: Any alteration of course needed to be large enough to be readily apparent to the watchkeeper on Ash

report_title: Boxford and Admiral Blake Report No 17/2011
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Visible contact absent from radar
- Range estimated without radar confirmation
Investigator finding: Failure to detect the fishing vessel by radar contributed to the master's continued overestimate of its range and surprise at its proximity.
Transferable lesson: Treat a visible but unpainted contact as unresolved range uncertainty, not evidence that it is distant.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific range-overestimation mechanism does not transfer where reliable independent ranging is available.
Source quotations:
- Page 5: the master’s inability to detect Admiral Blake by radar led to his continued inaccurate assessment that the fishing vessel was at a greater range than it actually was.

report_title: Boxford and Admiral Blake Report No 17/2011
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Only one of two available radars operating
- Unoptimised controls
- Suspected radar performance problems
- Single range scale monitored
Investigator finding: Using only one radar prevented simultaneous monitoring of different range scales. Incorrect settings were a plausible reason for non-detection, and doubts about performance strengthened the case for using both radars.
Transferable lesson: Optimise radar controls for the conditions and selected scale, and use available radar redundancy and complementary range scales when detection conditions or equipment performance are doubtful.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The dual-radar aspect does not transfer to vessels without a second operational radar.
Source quotations:
- Page 5: the use of only one of the two working radars prevented different range scales from being monitored simultaneously
- Page 5: the radar’s settings not being optimised for the prevailing sea state and the range scale selected.
- Page 6: the case for operating both radars, given the prevailing conditions, should have been even stronger.

report_title: Boxford and Admiral Blake Report No 17/2011
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- High vessel speed relative to lookout effectiveness
- Intermittent radar returns
- Sea or weather interference
Investigator finding: The radar lookout was inadequate for the vessel's speed; intermittent returns might have been missed because the display was not monitored frequently enough.
Transferable lesson: Match radar monitoring frequency and safe-speed assessment to detection limitations, interference and the time available at the vessel's speed.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report's particular speed is not a universal unsafe-speed threshold.
Source quotations:
- Page 5: the master and cadet were not monitoring the display sufficiently often, given their vessel’s speed
- Page 7: The radar lookout kept on board Boxford was inadequate given that the vessel’s speed was 19 knots.
- Page 6: the effect on radar detection of the sea state, weather and other sources of interference when determining safe speed.

report_title: MAIB Report 1/2021 - Minx and Vision - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact, unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable

- The proposed manoeuvre puts social expectations ahead of navigation or local speed restrictions.
Investigator finding: The skipper's perception of the charterer's wishes took priority over safe navigation and local speed restrictions.

report_title: MAIB Report 1/2021 - Minx and Vision - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: stationary_contact, unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- The vessel is heading directly towards a contact at speed.
- Safe clearance depends on a precisely timed last-moment manoeuvre.
- The proposal leaves no allowance for control failure or misjudgement.
Investigator finding: Heading directly towards Minx at speed left no margin for error, making any misjudgement, loss of control or material failure a high collision risk.
Transferable lesson: Do not accept a passing proposal whose safety depends on flawless last-moment execution; retain clearance and control margin for errors or failures.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This specific analogy does not transfer to an approach that retains adequate clearance and does not depend on a last-moment avoidance manoeuvre.
Source quotations:
- Page 6: Vision’s skipper then placed both yachts and their occupants in danger by effectively heading directly towards Minx at speed with no margin for error; during the approach any misjudgement, loss of control or material failure would create a high risk of collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, distraction
Warning signs:
- Watchkeeper leaving the wheelhouse
- Working position with virtually no external visibility
- Known approaching vessel
Investigator finding: From the shelter deck the skipper could neither maintain a proper lookout nor determine collision risk, despite having seen an approaching vessel.
Transferable lesson: Maintain effective lookout coverage when moving to work positions that prevent observation of approaching traffic.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The unattended-lookout analogy does not apply where effective lookout and risk assessment remain continuously provided.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: When the skipper left the wheelhouse and went to the shelter deck, from where he had virtually no external visibility, he could not maintain a proper lookout, or determine if a risk of collision existed.

Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Visual contact beyond the selected radar range
- No displayed radar contact despite an observed approaching light
Investigator finding: Increasing the fishing vessel's selected radar range would have provided information needed to assess CPA and collision risk.
Transferable lesson: Use a radar range that allows assessment of known approaching traffic rather than treating an empty short-range display as sufficient.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- Changing range alone does not address a contact absent for other reasons or provide a completed collision-risk assessment.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: Had the skipper increased the range set on his radar displays as required by COLREG Rule 7, this would have provided him with the information required to determine the CPA of Scot Explorer, and the risk of collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Small predicted passing margin
- Uncertainty in CPA estimation
- Ample sea room and no nearby shipping
Investigator finding: The accepted three-to-four-cable passing distance provided little safety margin, and early action to increase that margin was available with no other vessels nearby.
Transferable lesson: Assess the passing margin against measurement uncertainty and possible unexpected movement; use available room and time to establish a greater margin rather than accepting a marginal CPA.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report does not establish a universal minimum CPA.
- The available-action analogy must be reconsidered where other traffic or limited sea room constrains options.
Source quotations:

- Page 9: given that there were no other vessels in the vicinity, there was no reason why the chief officer or master could not have taken early action to provide a greater margin of safety.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: distraction, poor_monitoring, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Routine administration while a contact is close
- Sole watchkeeper diverted from observation
- Radar guard facility unused
Investigator finding: Routine administration interrupted monitoring as the vessels closed; alone and without the radar guard facility, the master remained unaware of the danger until seconds before impact.
Transferable lesson: Continue close-contact monitoring through CPA rather than allowing routine work to interrupt it; use available lookout and radar guard support without substituting them for proper observation.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This finding does not make radar guard alarms a replacement for a proper lookout.
- The close-contact priority is not a prohibition on all routine bridge work.
Source quotations:

- Page 9: the master’s preoccupation with routine administration distracted him from this important task.
