- Page 10: As this was not abnormal, the lookout was unaware that the chief officer had not registered his report.

report_title: Scot Isles and Wadi Halfa Report No 10/2009
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown

Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Radar targets visible but not acquired or plotted
- No developed assessment of target motion or collision risk
Investigator finding: ARPA was available but no targets were acquired or plotted, forfeiting an opportunity for early collision-risk assessment.
Transferable lesson: Use available radar plotting capability to develop an early assessment of collision risk rather than relying on an unanalysed radar display.

report_title: Scot Isles and Wadi Halfa Report No 10/2009
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Available AIS information not monitored
Investigator finding: The chief officer did not use the available AIS information about nearby vessels; investigators included this omission among the deficiencies in his watchkeeping.
Transferable lesson: Include available AIS contact information in situational awareness rather than leaving it unused, without treating it as a replacement for proper lookout.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not establish that AIS information is complete or accurate, or that a contact without AIS can be disregarded.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Radar observation interrupted by position-fixing duties.
- Contact first noticed at limited range despite serviceable radar.
Investigator finding: Failure to maintain a proper radar watch prevented early warning and timely avoidance; the radar lookout should have been continuous.
Transferable lesson: Maintain continuous radar surveillance in restricted visibility so developing collision risks are detected early enough for effective action.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific requirement for continuous radar surveillance is grounded here in restricted-visibility operations, not every clear-weather encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: The radar lookout should have been continuous
- Page 16: to keep a proper radar watch to obtain early warning of the risk of collision and take avoiding action in ample time.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other, poor_team_coordination
Warning signs:
- Automatic steering retained in poor visibility.
- No additional watch rating called for steering duties.
Investigator finding: The second officer should have changed from automatic to hand steering and called another watch rating.
Transferable lesson: Include steering mode and available helmsman support in poor-visibility readiness checks rather than deferring the transition until the final moments.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This finding concerns the poor-visibility circumstances described; it is not a general prohibition on automatic steering.
Source quotations:
- Page 18: The 2nd Officer should have changed from automatic to hand steering and called another watch rating to the bridge.
- Page 14: The failure to have the vessel on hand steering was a neglect of the ordinary practice of seamen, in the poor visibility prevailing.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Speed retained despite thick fog.
- Reliance on radar watch as sufficient protection.
Investigator finding: ZULFIKAR was not proceeding at a safe speed, and continuous radar monitoring would not have removed the need for immediate engine readiness.
Transferable lesson: Assess safe speed independently of confidence in radar monitoring; surveillance alone does not make the vessel's operating state safe in fog.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report supplies no universally safe speed or numerical speed threshold for another vessel or encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: The vessel was not proceeding at a safe speed.
- Page 14: Even if a continuous radar watch had been maintained the engines should still have been on stand-by ready for immediate manoeuvre.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Risk of collision apparent but no effective response initiated.
Investigator finding: No action was taken when the risk of collision had become apparent.
Transferable lesson: Once collision risk is apparent, move from observation to timely effective avoiding action rather than allowing the situation to continue unaddressed.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The finding does not identify one manoeuvre suitable for all future encounters; action must reflect the actual situation and available controls.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: No action was taken when it was apparent that risk of collision had developed.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Operating or fishing near the termination of a traffic separation scheme.
Investigator finding: Both vessels were required to exercise particular caution near the termination of the traffic scheme.
Transferable lesson: Treat proximity to a traffic-lane termination as a reason for heightened caution, including when fishing nearby rather than following the lane.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The location-specific analogy does not apply to an encounter remote from a traffic-scheme termination.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: There was a failure to navigate with particular caution, since the vessel was near the termination of the traffic lane.
- Page 19: WILHELMINA J was required to navigate with particular caution, since the fishing ground was near the termination of a traffic separation scheme.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, role_confusion
Warning signs:
- Fishing gear deployed.
- Developing close-quarters situation in fog.
- Expectation that the other vessel alone will act.
Investigator finding: In restricted visibility both vessels had an obligation to avoid a close-quarters situation; towing fishing gear should not have prevented effective action if detection and appraisal occurred early enough.
Transferable lesson: Do not treat fishing operations as a reason to wait for the other vessel in restricted visibility; detect and appraise threats early enough to preserve effective options.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report could not establish what WILHELMINA J detected or did.
- The capability assessment does not transfer to a vessel actually disabled or otherwise unable to manoeuvre.
Source quotations:
- Page 15: places an obligation on both vessels to take action to avoid a close quarters situation.
- Page 15: The fact that she was towing fishing gear should not have prevented her from taking effective avoiding action, provided ZULFIKAR was detected and the situation appraised at an early enough stage.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, recovery
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- A nearby echo assumed to be the vessel involved in contact.
- True course inferred from a brief relative-motion observation.
Investigator finding: The post-collision echo was probably the overtaking ship, and a brief observation of relative motion was inadequate to assess its approximate true course.
Transferable lesson: Maintain contact identity in multi-vessel situations and do not infer true motion or another vessel's safety from a brief, unverified echo observation.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific mistaken-identity mechanism does not transfer where contact identity is positively established and motion is adequately tracked.
Source quotations:
- Page 18: The echo which the Master saw on the starboard quarter by radar, after the collision, was probably that of the ship which had been overtaking ZULFIKAR.
- Page 18: It is doubtful that the Master could have assessed the approximate true course of the echo from a brief observation of its relative motion.

report_title: Sapphire II and Silver Chord Report No 21/2011.
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- A possible contact lies on a steady or nearly steady bearing ahead
- The radar heading marker could overlap the contact
Investigator finding: The radar heading marker might occasionally have obscured Sapphire II's target, but complete obscuration on every wheelhouse visit was highly unlikely.
Transferable lesson: Where the heading marker could mask a contact, account for that display limitation rather than treating a missed target as assurance that the sector is clear.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific masking analogy does not apply to contacts away from the heading marker.
- The investigation did not establish that marker masking actually caused the missed detection.
Source quotations:
- Page 7: it is possible the radar target of Sapphire II might have been occasionally obscured by the radar ship¶s head marker.
- Page 7: However, it is highly unlikely to have been completely obscured each time the skipper visited the wheelhouse.

report_title: Sapphire II and Silver Chord Report No 21/2011.
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- Shelters or deck fittings obstruct the view from the steering position
- Accommodation or the wheelhouse blocks the view from a deck working position
- Structural changes have reduced visibility without mitigation
Investigator finding: Both vessels had obstructed lookout positions; Silver Chord's shelter and equipment had reduced forward visibility without mitigating measures.
Transferable lesson: Assess actual sight lines from the positions used for navigation and deck work, and address blind sectors rather than assuming presence at those positions provides an effective lookout.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The obstruction-specific analogy does not apply where the relevant sectors are unobstructed or effectively covered by other lookout arrangements.

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: distraction, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Administrative work interrupts radar monitoring
- An initial traffic check appears clear
Investigator finding: Administrative duties distracted Talis’s chief officer from radar monitoring, delaying detection until the contact was less than one mile away.
Transferable lesson: Do not let an initially clear traffic picture justify interruptions to radar monitoring in restricted visibility; delayed detection consumes the time available for assessment and action.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The restricted-visibility analogy does not directly transfer where visual observation provides an effective continuous lookout.

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, poor_monitoring, delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Radar contact has no corresponding AIS transmission
- Visual confirmation is sought instead of tracking relative movement
Investigator finding: Reliance on AIS and attempts at visual confirmation displaced radar plotting, depriving the chief officer of relative-track and collision-risk information.
Transferable lesson: Assess a radar contact through plotting or systematic monitoring even when it has no AIS correlate; do not substitute a search for visual confirmation for relative-motion assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The missing-AIS mechanism does not apply when AIS correlation is available and independently checked; the plotting failure does not apply where equivalent systematic tracking is maintained.

- Page 8: By looking for the contact visually instead of plotting its relative movement on the radar, the C/O denied himself vital information about the relative track of the fishing vessel and the risk of collision.

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty

- Uncertain validity of a radar echo

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Very short time remaining at the observed closing speed
- Assumption that the other vessel will alter course
- Other vessel’s wheelhouse appears unmanned
Investigator finding: The chief officer continued watching in the mistaken expectation that Achieve would alter course; immediate action was required once its unmanned wheelhouse was seen at close range.
Transferable lesson: Do not spend the remaining avoidance window waiting for an assumed response from the other vessel, especially when observations indicate it may not be under an effective watch.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not establish give-way or stand-on roles, or prescribe a manoeuvre in a different encounter.

- Page 9: By the time Talis’s C/O saw that Achieve’s wheelhouse was unmanned, both vessels were close to each other and immediate action should have been taken to avoid a collision.

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Fog signals are not being made
- A fog signal is heard from an unseen vessel
Investigator finding: Fog signals could have alerted the vessels to each other, but hearing a signal would not reliably establish range, bearing, or collision risk.
Transferable lesson: Use required fog signals as an additional warning channel, and treat a heard signal as requiring immediate attention and action rather than as a substitute for collision-risk assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The fog-signal lesson is specific to operations in or near restricted visibility; a heard signal alone does not establish encounter geometry.
Source quotations:

- Page 8: While the aural detection of a fog signal would not have been an effective method of determining range and bearing, or of the risk of collision, it would have indicated that another vessel was close and that immediate action was required.

report_title: MAIB Report 14/2021 - Achieve/Talis - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: restricted_visibility
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- Other vessel’s intentions are uncertain
- Warning-signal operation competes with taking control
- No watchkeeper is visible on the other vessel
Investigator finding: The long whistle blast was less appropriate than the doubt signal, and reaching its control delayed manual helm action despite little prospect of a swift response from Achieve.
Transferable lesson: Use an appropriate warning signal without allowing its operation, or an expectation of response, to delay urgent collision-avoidance control actions.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific signal comparison concerns vessels in sight with uncertainty about intentions; the control-location delay depends on bridge layout and current control state.
Source quotations:
- Page 9: Given the C/O’s uncertainty of Achieve’s intentions, the sounding of one long blast on the ship’s whistle was less appropriate than five short and rapid blasts
- Page 9: with no-one in the fishing vessel’s wheelhouse there was little prospect of a swift reaction and using the whistle control, located on the port side of the bridge, delayed the C/O changing the helm to manual control and putting the rudder to starboard.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- A shore information service acknowledges a proposed passage through traffic.
Investigator finding: CNIS supplied information and monitored traffic, but did not control vessels or issue instructions.
Transferable lesson: Do not treat an information service's acknowledgement as traffic-control clearance or a substitute for onboard collision-risk assessment.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The precise service limitation does not transfer to a service with explicitly different traffic-control authority.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: CNIS does not issue instructions to vessels in the Strait and is in no sense a traffic control system.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment
Warning signs:
- Radar echoes merge or appear to coincide.
- Relative tracks depend on qualitative interpretation of limited-resolution radar records.
Investigator finding: The reconstructed radar tracks were not absolutely precise or comprehensive, and merged echoes alone did not establish collision or a dangerously close passing.
Transferable lesson: Carry radar discrimination and track uncertainty into proximity assessments; an apparent echo merger is not a precise measurement of passing distance.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report's specific resolution limitation cannot be assumed for every radar or tracking system.
- This finding does not establish that an apparent merger is safe.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: the tracks shown cannot be considered as absolutely precise or comprehensive
- Page 9: this merging of echoes does not, in itself, demonstrate that collision or even a dangerously close passing occurred
- Page 9: the radar discrimination is not sufficiently precise for this

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- A vessel appears stopped on a ground-referenced radar plot while a significant tidal stream is running.
Investigator finding: Although OCEAN HOUND appeared stopped on the plot, the investigators assessed that she was making way through the water at about the tidal-stream speed.
Transferable lesson: Distinguish ground-referenced motion from motion through the water when interpreting a stopped target or evaluating the vessel's motion state in current.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific inference does not transfer without a known motion reference and relevant current information.
- A stopped ground track alone does not establish engine or steering settings.
Source quotations:
- Page 8: in the few minutes before her echo disappears is shown as being stopped
- Page 8: as the tide was setting NE'ly at just over 2 knots she will in fact have been making way at about that speed
- Page 9: through the water.

report_title: MAIB Report No 13/2014 - Endurance - Very Serious Marine Casualty
text:
MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency, recovery
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, other
Warning signs:
- Close approach to the leeward side of a drifting vessel.
- Wind and waves can set the other vessel towards own vessel.
- Rough seas produce substantial relative vessel motion.
Investigator finding: Although heading into wind and sea possibly provided a more stable platform, the risk of the drifting cruiser being set towards the tug at close quarters was significant and predictable.
Transferable lesson: Assess drift and relative vessel motion before accepting a close approach; improved own-vessel stability or apparent shelter does not remove the risk of contact.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific leeward-side analogy does not transfer where the contact is not drifting under wind and waves.
- This finding does not determine COLREG roles or a manoeuvre for a normal underway encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 14: Heading into the wind and sea possibly made Endurance a more stable platform
- Page 14: Nonetheless, the risk of Sirius M being set towards Endurance when the veVVelV were cloVe waV Vignificant and predictable.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: inadequate_cpa_assessment, other
Warning signs:
- More than one vessel within radar range
- Uncertain correspondence between a visual contact and an acquired radar target
Investigator finding: The investigators considered it possible, rather than established, that the mate confused LUC with another radar target.
Transferable lesson: Where several contacts are present, verify that radar-derived motion and CPA information belong to the vessel being assessed visually.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report did not establish that target confusion occurred.
- This particular analogy does not transfer where contact identity is unambiguous and verified.
Source quotations:
- Page 10: it is possible that the mate mistook LUC for the target he observed on the radar

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: distraction, poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Chart work or scheduled log entries competing with contact monitoring
- OOW attention concentrated at the chart table
Investigator finding: Plotting the position and completing the log displaced the more important tasks of lookout and monitoring the other vessel.
Transferable lesson: Prioritise lookout and contact monitoring over routine chart and log work; defer the full entry when necessary rather than interrupting surveillance.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This task-priority analogy does not apply when chart or log work does not interrupt an effective lookout.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: The more important task of maintaining a proper lookout and monitoring the other vessel became secondary
- Page 12: The position could then have been plotted on the charts, and an entry made in the deck log book later

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action
Warning signs:
- Collision courses recognised
- Attempts to establish VHF contact consuming response time
Investigator finding: The skipper lost valuable time attempting VHF contact instead of making the appropriate sound signal early.
Transferable lesson: When the situation calls for an appropriate warning sound signal, make it promptly rather than allowing VHF contact attempts to delay it.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This finding does not establish that all VHF use is inappropriate.
- The sound-signal lesson applies where such a signal is appropriate to the encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: he should have made the appropriate sound signal in ample time
- Page 12: rather than waste valuable time trying to make contact by VHF radio

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: stand_on
Encounter phases: action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: delayed_action, ineffective_action
Warning signs:
- Continuing convergence without effective action by the other vessel
- Avoiding action postponed until very close range
Investigator finding: LUC's avoiding action was not taken in ample time and did not prevent the collision.
Transferable lesson: Do not allow stand-on status to postpone necessary avoiding action until there is insufficient time for it to be effective.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This lesson does not prescribe a particular manoeuvre or establish when another encounter reaches the action threshold.
- The stand-on analogy requires that status to be established independently.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: Although action was taken in accordance with Rule 17(a)(ii) and (b) of the Collision Regulations, it was not made in ample time
- Page 12: The subsequent action taken by the skipper was not effective in preventing a collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: not_applicable
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Proposed close approach without an operational or emergency reason
- Willingness to allow another vessel alongside merely for observation
Investigator finding: The investigators described coming close alongside, or allowing it, for non-operational and non-emergency reasons as extremely hazardous.
Transferable lesson: Avoid discretionary close-alongside approaches and do not accept them as harmless merely because they have happened before.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The stated finding expressly distinguishes operational reasons and emergencies; it does not assess the acceptability of a particular approach in those circumstances.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: Coming close alongside a vessel, or allowing another vessel to come close alongside,
- Page 12: for other than operational reasons or in an emergency, is extremely hazardous and contravenes the Collision Regulations

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Wheelhouse blind sectors or restricted sightlines
- Reliance on good weather or bridge manning as evidence of an effective lookout
Investigator finding: Design restrictions seriously hampered lookout in both vessels, and neither took sufficient steps to overcome them. Both remained unaware of the other until effective avoiding action was no longer possible.
Transferable lesson: Assess whether lookout arrangements actually cover restricted sightlines; good visibility and a manned wheelhouse do not by themselves establish adequate contact awareness.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The design-restriction aspect does not transfer where sightlines are unobstructed and effective lookout coverage is established.
- This finding does not establish a particular avoiding manoeuvre for a detected contact.
Source quotations:
- Page 1: neither vessel was aware of the other until too late to take effective avoiding action; and this was the main cause of the collision.
- Page 1: visibility from the wheelhouse was seriously restricted and in neither vessel were sufficient steps taken to overcome this difficulty.
- Page 1: it was a fine moonlit night and in both vessels the wheelhouse was properly manned

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, poor_team_coordination
Warning signs:
- A lookout sees a close contact that has not been reported to the wheelhouse
- Reporting is conditional on the lookout personally perceiving danger
- A close parallel passage is accepted as routine
Investigator finding: The forward seamen saw MARCHIONESS but did not report her because they perceived no danger, consistent with their normal reporting practice. Nobody in BOWBELLE's wheelhouse saw her before collision; the report identified lookout failure as a principal cause.
Transferable lesson: Do not make reporting a close contact dependent solely on the lookout's own judgment that it is hazardous; the conning team needs that information to assess the developing encounter.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The communication-gap analogy does not apply where the conning team already has timely, reliable awareness of the contact.
- The passage does not establish a universal reporting range or CPA threshold.
Source quotations:
- Page 4: They apprehended no danger and made no report to the wheelhouse; this accorded with their normal practice of only reporting when hazard was perceived.
- Page 4: No-one in BOWBELLE's wheelhouse saw MARCHIONESS at all before the collision.
- Page 1: neither vessel was aware of the other until too late to take effective avoiding action; and this was the main cause of the collision.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Overtaking without effective awareness of the vessel being passed
Investigator finding: The report particularly emphasised BOWBELLE's lookout failure because, as the overtaking vessel, she had the overriding duty to keep clear.
Transferable lesson: When overtaking, maintain the contact awareness needed to fulfil the duty to keep clear; failure to detect the other vessel does not remove that responsibility.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The role-specific lesson does not transfer unless the vessel is established to be overtaking.
- It does not determine responsibilities in a crossing or head-on encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 1: The failure in look-out, especially in BOWBELLE who, as the overtaking vessel had the over- riding duty to keep clear

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- A channel is assumed clear without an effective lookout
- Channel positioning relies on that assumption
Investigator finding: MARCHIONESS's failure to keep to the starboard side of the channel was a major contributory factor, linked to lookout failure and her skipper's belief that the channel was clear.
Transferable lesson: Do not treat an inadequately observed channel as clear or use that assumption to justify departing from applicable channel-positioning requirements.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The channel-positioning lesson does not transfer to waters without an applicable channel-positioning requirement.
- It does not prescribe a course alteration in a different encounter.
Source quotations:
- Page 1: A further major contributory factor was the failure of MARCHIONESS to keep to the starboard side of the channel
- Page 1: this is linked to the failure of look- out in that her Skipper plainly thought that the channel was clear.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: overtaking_vessel, uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- A large vessel overtaking a smaller vessel at close separation
- Unexpected sheer of the smaller vessel
Investigator finding: Hydrodynamic interaction was highly likely to have caused, and probably principally caused, MARCHIONESS to sheer across BOWBELLE's bow; at very close separation the smaller vessel can lose control.
Transferable lesson: Include interaction-induced sheer and loss of control in the risk assessment for close overtaking between markedly different-sized vessels, rather than assuming both will retain their present tracks.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This specific mechanism is not established here for widely separated vessels or materially different encounter geometry.
Source quotations:
- Page 4: when, as here, a relatively large ship is overtaking a smaller one the latter will tend to sheer across the bow of the former.
- Page 4: Where the two vessels are very close the effect can be so great that the small vessel loses all control.
- Page 4: It is highly likely that this effect was a cause, probably the major cause, of MARCHIONESS sheering across the bow of BOWBELLE.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Speed through the water substantially exceeds speed over ground
- Strong current during a close passing encounter
Investigator finding: The tide made the vessels' speeds through the water substantially greater than their speeds over ground, and interaction depended strongly on speed through the water.
Transferable lesson: Use speed through the water, not ground speed alone, when assessing hydrodynamic interaction risk in current.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The distinction has little practical significance where current is negligible; this passage does not provide a universal interaction threshold.
Source quotations:
- Page 4: their speed through the water was substantially more than that over the ground, and the effect of interaction is very dependent upon speed through the water.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Traffic movement broadcasts relevant to the vessel's intended passage
- Departure without monitoring available navigation broadcasts
Investigator finding: Movement broadcasts could have provided advance warning, including before departure; even the final broadcast could have prompted a timely look astern.
Transferable lesson: Monitor available navigation broadcasts before departure and underway, and turn relevant traffic information into an active lookout check rather than merely receiving it.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This lesson does not assume that broadcasts identify every contact or replace direct lookout.
Source quotations:
- Page 9: If any of these transmissions were received, they ought to have been recognised as providing a warning.
- Page 9: if it had led to the Skipper of MARCHIONESS looking astern as soon as he heard it.
- Page 9: if it had been monitored as would have been wise with the vessel about to leave, would have given good advance warning.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Habitual use of central bridge arches
- Assumption that smaller craft can always use side arches
Investigator finding: The report found widespread disregard of the fairway requirement, but accepted that blanket segregation through side arches was impracticable because their availability depended on vessel and tide.
Transferable lesson: Assess fairway use against applicable requirements and actual navigability, rather than habitual central passage or an assumption that smaller craft always have an alternative arch.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The local bridge and bye-law details apply to the Thames described in the report; they do not establish equivalent requirements elsewhere.
Source quotations:
- Page 12: Clearly, Rule 9 was widely ignored on the River.
- Page 12: For many such craft, and for much of the time (depending on the state of the tide) the side arches are not passable

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Restricted visibility aft or persistent wheelhouse blind arcs
- A contact may remain outside the navigator's view throughout its approach
Investigator finding: Restricted wheelhouse visibility prevented detection of approaching vessels in earlier similar accidents; BOWBELLE's blind arc probably concealed MARCHIONESS for virtually the entire relevant period.
Transferable lesson: Arrange lookout coverage to compensate for blind arcs, including astern; absence of a sighting from the conning position is not evidence that the area is clear.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific blind-arc mechanism does not apply where the relevant sector is continuously and effectively observed.
Source quotations:
- Page 1: the failure of the launch to see the ship coming up on her from astern, apparently because of lack of visibility from her wheelhouse
- Page 8: the launch was in the blind arc from the wheelhouse for virtually the entire time that she ought to have been in view.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking, multi_contact
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring
Warning signs:
- Planning passage around one contact without awareness of another
- Reliance on priority arrangements despite incomplete traffic awareness
Investigator finding: The report doubted that stronger regulations would have prevented MARCHIONESS's channel choice because her skipper was unaware of BOWBELLE while overtaking HURLINGHAM.
Transferable lesson: Do not treat compliance with passage-priority arrangements as a substitute for establishing which vessels are present before choosing a route around another contact.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This does not determine priorities or permissible routes in another jurisdiction.
- The specific awareness failure is absent when all relevant contacts are detected and assessed.
Source quotations:
- Page 3: the fundamental point that MARCHIONESS was unaware of the other ship’s presence
- Page 3: her Skipper would probably still have used channel, legitimately as it would have seemed to him even under stronger Regulations, so as to overtake HURLINGHAM.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, emergency
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Very close passage between a larger ship and smaller craft
- Unexpected yaw or loss of control of the smaller craft
Investigator finding: The report considered interaction likely to have been the major factor in MARCHIONESS swinging farther across BOWBELLE's bow, probably augmented by contact.
Transferable lesson: When assessing a very close pass, allow for interaction potentially disturbing the smaller vessel's control rather than assuming both vessels will maintain their intended tracks.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The report supplies no universal interaction threshold or safe passing distance.
- The precise contributions of interaction, contact and attempted avoiding action remained uncertain.
Source quotations:
- Page 6: interaction between the two vessels may have led to loss of control of the smaller craft and caused the swing
- Page 6: interaction is likely to have been the major factor, probably augmented by physical contact

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Course estimates based on oblique visual observation
Investigator finding: The report cautioned that visual course estimates are difficult when a vessel is not directly ahead or astern of the observer.
Transferable lesson: Treat oblique visual estimates of another vessel's course alteration with appropriate uncertainty rather than as precise measured changes.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- This specific limitation does not establish the accuracy or inaccuracy of instrument-derived tracks.
Source quotations:
- Page 6: it is very difficult to judge by eye the course of a vessel not directly ahead or astern of the observer

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing, action_required
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Close parallel tracks
- Course changes near bridge transits
- Previously non-converging tracks beginning to converge
Investigator finding: Initially parallel courses would have produced a close but safe overtaking passage, but the courses converged shortly before impact.
Transferable lesson: Reassess a close passing situation when either vessel's course changes; an earlier non-converging assessment does not establish that the developing passage remains safe.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific transition described does not apply where courses and separation remain stable without convergence.
Source quotations:
- Page 2: Until shortly before the collision, the two vessels were heading on parallel courses which, had they been continued, would have led to BOWBELLE overtaking MARCHIONESS close but safely.
- Page 2: Within about half a minute before impact, however, their courses began to converge.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: overtaking
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: risk_developing, action_required, emergency
Causal mechanisms: other
Warning signs:
- Very close passage between vessels
- Converging tracks
- Unexpected yaw
- Tidal set
Investigator finding: Hydrodynamic interaction caused MARCHIONESS to lose control at close quarters, and the tide then set her onto BOWBELLE's bow.
Transferable lesson: When assessing very close passing margins, account for interaction and tidal effects rather than assuming that commanded headings will remain controllable.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The specific loss-of-control analogy does not transfer where separation and vessel circumstances make hydrodynamic interaction immaterial or where tidal set is absent.
Source quotations:
- Page 3: On their now converging courses, the vessels came so close that in MARCHIONESS control was lost due to interaction and the vessel sheared strongly to port across the tide which set her on to BOWBELLE’s bow.

MAIB INVESTIGATION LESSON CARD
Encounter types: unknown
Vessel roles: uncertain
Encounter phases: monitoring, risk_developing
Causal mechanisms: poor_monitoring, other
Warning signs:
- Navigation lights against numerous background lights
- Lights difficult to see at close range
- Unidentified visual contact
Investigator finding: Background lights may have prevented vessel recognition, and BOWBELLE's light placement and construction reduced close-range visibility, despite required lights being shown.
Transferable lesson: In a cluttered light background, actively search for and identify vessels; compliance with lighting requirements does not by itself ensure that a contact will be conspicuous.
Do not transfer this analogy when:
- The background-light and light-placement analogy does not apply where contacts are clearly visible and positively identified.
Source quotations:
- Page 3: It is possible that BOWBELLE was seen at a distance but not noticed, also because of the background of other lights; and not seen when close at hand because her navigation lights were insufficiently visible, due to their placing and her construction.
- Page 3: However, she would have been visible to a careful and searching look.
- Page 3: There is no suggestion that either vessel was not showing the lights as required.
